sections.h2: Fastest way to sell in Oshkosh
sections.html:
Get your documents in order before choosing a buyer. Three things deserve attention at the start: what your address shows in the city's permit records, your condition report, and a deed that can be recorded the day you close. After that, condition decides whether a listing or a cash sale fits.

  1. Open the city's electronic property file for your address and read the permits and code cases.
  2. Complete the Wisconsin Real Estate Condition Report in advance, ready to send on acceptance day.
  3. Request a payoff figure from your lender and save a copy of this year's tax bill.
  4. Choose among an agent, a sale on your own, or written cash offers that show their fees and closing date.
  5. Decide who prepares the deed and files the electronic transfer return.

Cash can shrink the middle steps because no mortgage appraisal usually stands in the way. None of the steps vanishes entirely.

Winnebago County's seat, Oshkosh, has about 67,460 residents and 27,451 households, with 55.0 percent of homes owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $177,700. Owners with a mortgage typically pay $1,362 a month and those without pay $635. Gross rent has a median of $935, and household income a median of $62,188. Use those as background only, because recent sales near your address say more about price than a citywide median.

With a University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh campus downtown, some buyers think about renting to students. Two city rules apply. No more than four unrelated people may share one living unit unless the dwelling operates as a rooming house. And parking on lawns or unmarked areas in the university area brings citations of $232 per day. If your house has been a rental, collect any inspection records for the buyer. The city's rental inspections page covers complaints and inspections.

Your Oshkosh bill combines levies from the city, the county, the Oshkosh Area School District and Fox Valley Technical College. The assessor neither issues bills nor sets the rate, so a levy increase or a referendum can push your tax up while your assessed value stays flat. Special assessments and unpaid utility bills may also show up on a bill. Clear them before a buyer's title company finds them.

Think your value is wrong? Begin with Open Book, then go to the Board of Review. The City Clerk provides the objection form, and the request has to arrive at least 48 hours before the Board meets. A December tax bill is too late to start. Five regular members and two alternates, serving five-year terms, make up the Board, and it considers only evidence presented at the hearing, such as recent comparable sales. For the next cycle, phone the assessor at (920) 236-5070.

Inspection Services handles Oshkosh building permits, and applications are now online. Work that can need a permit includes new construction, additions, remodels, garages and sheds, decks and porches, siding and roofing, doors and windows other than sash replacement, electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling, pools, fences, patios, driveways and demolition. Painting inside, new flooring and a replaced faucet do not. Work cannot start until the permit is issued and paid for.

Two rules trip up sellers. Tearing down anything, even a garage, first requires a plumbing permit to disconnect water and sewer. And new shingles may sit over no more than one layer of old ones. The city also maintains electronic property files of permits, cases and projects, though records before 1997 are still being scanned. Call 920-236-5048 to learn whether your address is complete. Ask which fee schedule applies when you pull a permit.

Selling a home of one to four units under Wis. Stat. 709.02 means handing the buyer a finished Real Estate Condition Report inside 10 days of acceptance. Once those 10 days end, a buyer still waiting has two business days to rescind and get deposits back. Fiduciaries appointed by a court who never occupied the property are excused by Wis. Stat. 709.01, and so are transfers that owe no transfer fee.

Answer every item and keep a copy for your own records. If a late-discovered problem changes an answer before closing, tell your title company or attorney right away.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Winnebago County
sections.html:
Your deed is filed with the Winnebago County Register of Deeds, which checks four things on the page: a notarized grantor signature, a legal description, a return address and, beneath it, the tax-bill parcel number. Photocopies do not qualify. The office wants the original, signed originally, along with the receipt from the electronic transfer return. Phone 920-232-3394 with questions.

Winnebago County Register of Deeds charges
ServiceCharge
Deed or other standard document$30 flat
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page
Certified copyAdd $1 for the certificate
State transfer fee$3 per $1,000 of value, rounded up to the next hundred

The seller bears the transfer fee, which Wis. Stat. 77.22 creates. You can pay by cash, money order or personal check. A card is accepted only for orders placed in the office, and adds a $2.50 surcharge on amounts up to $50.

Use the first 10 days for four jobs. Send the condition report. Check your permit file against the city's records. Get a payoff figure from your lender and a copy of the tax bill. Then settle who drafts the deed. A title company or attorney usually does, and the Register of Deeds expects the original with original signatures.

Close to the closing date, file the transfer return online and bring its receipt with the deed. A cash buyer takes the loan out of this timeline, though not the report, the return or the recording.

The Oshkosh Area School District operates two high schools, Oshkosh North and Oshkosh West. Fox Valley Technical College also has a local campus. Parents will ask which school covers your address, so confirm it and name it in the listing.

Investors will ask about tenants, so put leases, rent rolls and any inspection records in one folder, and tell them which units are occupied before they have to ask. Students and other renters are a big part of this market, and a buyer who plans to keep tenants in place will want to see the paperwork before making an offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Oshkosh rental with students in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Read the lease first and give the buyer the facts. The city caps an ordinary living unit at four unrelated occupants unless it operates as a rooming house, and parking citations in the university area run $232 per day.

faqs.q: Who sets the tax rate on my Oshkosh bill?
faqs.a: Four bodies: the City of Oshkosh, Winnebago County, the Oshkosh Area School District and Fox Valley Technical College. The city assessor neither sets the rate nor issues bills.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Oshkosh assessment?
faqs.a: Go to Open Book, then the Board of Review. Ask the City Clerk for an objection form at least 48 hours before the Board meets, because a December tax bill is too late. The assessor's line is (920) 236-5070.

faqs.q: Will Winnebago County record a photocopy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. It records only the original with original signatures. The grantor's signature must be notarized, and the electronic transfer return receipt must be filed first and brought in with the deed and the $30 fee.

faqs.q: How do I find permits on my Oshkosh house?
faqs.a: Call Inspection Services at 920-236-5048. The city keeps electronic property files covering permits, cases and projects. Records before 1997 are still being scanned, so staff can say whether your address is complete.
